notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

phase_0.boundary_condition: the finite initial segment of N under test
phase_0.domain_name: A subseteq N with divergent reciprocal sum contains arbitrarily
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: enumeration of subset elements in increasing order
AFWD.justification: it moves from smaller to larger natural numbers toward the target segment

AREV.chosen_element: descent from n to 1 through candidate starting points
AREV.justification: it reverses the enumeration to test each possible progression origin

CLINK.chosen_element: composition of reciprocal accumulation with progression detection
CLINK.justification: the sum over the subset and the scan for arithmetic progressions are chained as one test

ENGAGR.chosen_element: subset with divergent reciprocal sum and no long progression
ENGAGR.justification: the divergence condition and the absence of progressions hold simultaneously as a live contradiction

EVALF.chosen_element: segment contains no progression of the target length
EVALF.justification: the negative arm refutes the progression property

EVALT.chosen_element: segment contains an arbitrarily long arithmetic progression
EVALT.justification: the affirmative arm establishes the progression property

FFUSE.chosen_element: the combined verdict over the segment
FFUSE.justification: the divergent and convergent arms rejoin into one resolved state over SIXTEEN_3

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the test on the current finite segment
FSPLIT.justification: it opens into the arm where the reciprocal sum diverges and the arm where it converges

IFIX.justification: the witness is appended permanently and cannot be undone

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the subset as a self-identifying collection
IMSCRIB.justification: the subset is recognized as itself without transformation during membership checks

TANCH.chosen_element: the closed interval [1, n] of N
TANCH.justification: it bounds the search space and contains every candidate element and progression

VINIT.justification: no elements are named and no sum or progression exists yet

phase_2.fuse_element: the combined verdict over the segment
phase_2.fuse_result: a single resolved state over SIXTEEN_3 recording whether the segment carries a long progression under each sum regime
phase_2.rejoin_note: the divergent arm scans for progressions while the convergent arm scans for progressions; the arms rejoin into one state, and the fork does not stay open
phase_2.split_element: the test on the current finite segment
phase_2.split_input: the finite initial segment of N with the subset intersected
split_outputs: reciprocal sum over the segment diverges
reciprocal sum over the segment converges
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: a live contradiction, the paraconsistent resolution
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: uninitialized, nothing established

steps.domain_action: empty subset of N with no elements named
enumerate subset elements in increasing order through the segment
branch on whether the reciprocal sum over the segment diverges or converges
the divergent arm finds an arithmetic progression of the target length
the divergent arm finds no arithmetic progression of the target length
the convergent arm finds an arithmetic progression of the target length
the convergent arm finds no arithmetic progression of the target length
hold the divergent sum with no long progression as a live contradiction
rejoin the divergent and convergent arms into one resolved state over SIXTEEN_3
descend from n to 1 testing each candidate starting point for a progression
compose reciprocal accumulation with progression detection across the segment
recognize the subset as itself during membership checks
append the counterexample subset permanently to the record
seal the closed interval [1, n] as the boundary containing the whole test

phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical list of known subsets with divergent reciprocal sums
phase_5.compiler_frontend: translates the subset and progression test into the IMASM token word
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: passes segment bounds and partial sums between the enumeration and scan components
phase_5.memory_mechanism: stores the subset elements and the running reciprocal sum in append-only registers
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: orders the enumeration before the split and the scan after the split

phase_6.cycle_cost: one reciprocal term and one progression check per element per cycle
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — each element is enumerated once and each arm performs a bounded scan, so the cycle is entropy-conservative
